summary: Submitting the authority-transition control that was prepared but not previously submitted, with execution requested. It is a new investigation with its own experiment: in the three-node Node-API cluster with StepDownOnRemoval enabled, node 1 is elected, a follower proposes the removal of node 1, the harness records whether the removed leader steps down together with its state, membership and leader view, then advances the clock in rounds with delivery between rounds until some node reports itself leader, and finally proposes a payload on that leader and checks whether it commits. Three comparisons cover the step-down with a not-equal-zero assertion for the new leader and a present assertion for the committed payload, so the new leader's identity is not pinned to a specific node. A local run shows the documented sequence exactly: node 1 becomes StateFollower with voter false and no leader, node 2 emerges as the new leader while nodes 1 and 3 are followers, and the payload proposed on node 2 is committed and observed on the two remaining voters, which is consistent with the removed node no longer being part of the configuration. This closes the last configuration-option axis the audit had not exercised; its receipt will be interpreted next.
